The parent dp01 still first captures411 onA and215 onB, despite4/4 local wins.
Its champion-A first100 central damage is1080. Sparse telemetry and fuel events

Immediately after the kill, live info disappears (known1->0,position(-1,-1)),

Current committed World::refresh uses:
`c.is_visible() ? (c.is_alive()?c.health():0) : c.base_stats().base_health`.
The exact observed live-info sequence yields estimates5880 at29,5770 at30,
then5880 after the partial kill34: the dead member is restored to120 design HP.
A native fixture executing the actual parent World::refresh and task_expired
reproduces progress30 and stall expiry38. Nonlethal10->5 damage at34 refreshes
progress34 and prevents38 expiry. The fixture uses scripted host visibility,
not a claim of directly reading private release memory or measuring fuel.

SDK `camp::is_visible()` probes live sdk_camp info and returns false on not-found
or not-in-vision. `camp::state()/is_dead()` uses sdk_camp_state and can still
report dead when the last occupied tile is visible. Checked-in SDK typed_api.cpp
explicitly tests a dead state while !is_visible(), then throws after hiding its
tile. Rules say camps do not chase. Do not equate lack of live info with death:
hidden living camps must retain the original conservative design-HP fallback.

Hypothesis: correctly contributing zero for a locally verified dead member
prevents a real kill from increasing the remaining-work estimate, allowing
normal task progress/commitment to persist. Remaining failures may include
expensive host queries, other task changes or execution cost. No timer increase,
fake attack-progress stamp, permanent commitment or cached omniscient deaths.

## Narrow production contract

Only production `objectives.cpp`, in committed-task remaining HP refresh, may
change. Preserve the existing visible/live branch and all surrounding refresh
scheduling, group lifecycle, reward/capture/respawn and progress comparison rules.
On the existing !c.is_visible() branch, if its cached spawn tile is in the
current snapshot's visibility and a permitted state query positively reports
dead, contribute0 instead of design HP. Otherwise contribute original base HP.
Never query hidden health; live info unavailable is not itself proof of death.
The current snapshot/round must still be usable for this new dead-state probe:
check its round both before and after that new query. If the query crosses a
round, retain baseHP even if it returned dead. Add no round query to the already
visible branch. This is a guard on the new inference, not a refresh-wide rewrite.
If its new state probe fails with api_not_in_vision or api_not_found, conservatively
retain base HP; do not swallow unrelated SDK errors. Document this uncertainty
fallback rather than pretending all missing identities are known dead.

No new persistent member cache, additional path field, new host query on the
already-visible branch, camp score/solo-clear change, task timer change, combat
change or logging. Noncommitted objectives retain existing design-health policy.
Keep this a local remaining-work observation correction, not a broader refresh
or fuel-budget redesign. Extra queries on visible dead tiles can change release
timing; report that risk and preserve exact source/artifact identity.

- New state lookup not-in-vision/not-found or stale round cannot invent known

Tests establish the observation contract, not full engine performance. List host
substitutions, tests actually run and remaining limitations in IMPLEMENTATION.md.
